page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-48 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor featuring 24 physical cores and 48 dedicated vCPUs with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance includes 192.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support covers AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, though AVX-512 extensions and AMX are not supported. This configuration does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, relying instead on network-attached persistent storage.

Benchmark data demonstrates strong compute capacity across multi-threaded scenarios. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieved a single-core score of 2696.37 and a multi-core score of 64799.72, placing both in the top 25%. PassMark testing yielded a CPU mark of 51314.0 and an encryption score of 51408.75, both ranking in the top tier, complemented by a strong PassMark memory score of 2819.89. Geekbench tests measured a single-core score of 1515.0 and a multi-core score of 14504.0, accompanied by strong results in ray tracing (51174.0) and image processing (13726.0).

Throughput benchmarks reflect steady mid-tier execution. Large-block uncached memory transfers registered 109.91 GB/sec for reads and 57.35 GB/sec for writes. The instance recorded 47.2 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks, 31.27 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 85.49 GB/sec. On CPU-based large language model inference, it processed 1813.12 prompt tokens per second and generated 288.49 tokens per second using a 135M model, tapering to 95.99 prompt tokens and 23.18 generation tokens per second on a 7B model.

With its 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, n2d-standard-48 offers high resource density and balanced compute capacity for scale. The absence of local disk requires planning for external storage performance, but the hardware profile is well suited for enterprise web serving, relational databases, continuous integration build clusters, and parallel data processing jobs.
